correctness.rationale: For a fort, each rim vertex in X forces its attached leaf; each outside rim with exactly one rim-neighbor in X forces its leaf; with two rim-neighbors, an optional selected leaf can be removed, so no minimal fort contains it. This yields canonical B(X) for every nonempty X. A proper subfort B(Y) contained in B(X) exists precisely if membership of Y is equal at the two selected neighbors of each missing intermediate rim index; equivalently Y is a union of connected components of the graph H_X on X. Thus minimal forts are exactly those whose H_X is connected. With n even, H_X edges preserve parity and connected supports are cyclic intervals of a parity class; with n odd, step-two order is a single n-cycle, and supported intervals have length <=(n+1)/2, giving the parity formulas. Independently enumerated all 2^(2n)-1 nonempty subsets of actual cycle-corona graphs for n=3..8, tested the original outside-neighbor predicate, inclusion minimality by subforts, obtaining M_n=(6,6,15,14,28,26). Independently checked the exact n=6 counterexample X={0,1,3,4} is minimal in C6; its standard lift contains strict fort B({1,3})={v1,v3,w0,w1,w3,w4}. This refutes the v1 statement, not any uninspected later revision.

value.rationale: Minimal forts are the natural primitive obstructions for zero forcing. The sunlet is a canonical corona/cycle family, and the unexpectedly quadratic rather than exponential minimal-fort census gives a complete classification rather than a toy example. The six-cycle counterexample explains precisely why a natural general lifting argument fails and prevents propagation of an incorrect lower bound. An exact count plus structural correspondence are separately useful.

limitations: Finite simple sunlets n>=3, vertex-labeled minimal forts; no arbitrary corona or automorphism quotient
No claim that all general 2024-paper graph results are false; only identified v1 Proposition23 lifting and Corollary24 application
